status: prespecified; written and committed before Gate 0 and before any LLM call. Changes only via dated addenda in docs/protocol.md.

data.survey: CDC BRFSS 2025 LLCP (combined landline + cell) public-use file

reference.dataset: Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS) Prevalence Data (2011 to present)
reference.statistic: Crude Prevalence only (the only data_value_type published for 2025)

gate0.estimator: weighted proportion; Taylor-linearization variance, with-replacement PSUs, full-design domain estimation; single-PSU strata contribute 0; Wald 95% CI p +/- 1.96 SE

cell_sets.G0_primary: every P&T 2025 question x response in catalog/indicators.json (55 questions) x 50 jurisdictions (47 states + DC + GU + PR), break_out = Overall, excluding cells where CDC publishes no value
cell_sets.G0_breakout: same questions x responses x jurisdictions x 29 break_out values (Sex, Age Group incl. 65-74/75+, Race/Ethnicity, Education Attained, Household Income), excluding cells with no CDC value
cell_sets.G0_median: US (all states, DC, territories) and UW (all states and DC) median rows, Overall, point estimate only

sub_checks: suppression decision agreement (denominator n < 50 or RSE > 0.3)
gate0.cell_reproduced: point AND ci_low AND ci_high within tolerance (median cells: point only)
gate0.indicator_flag: any indicator with < 95% of its G0_primary cells reproduced is flagged and investigated
gate0.disclosed_prior_look: During method validation one cell (WA, _RFHLTH, Fair or Poor Health, Overall) was computed and matched CDC (17.31 [16.64, 17.98]) before this protocol was written.

tool_scope.geography: one of 50 jurisdictions, or US_MEDIAN (P&T 'US'), or STATES_DC_MEDIAN (P&T 'UW')
tool_scope.national_convention: Questions about 'the US' / 'nationally' are answered with the CDC P&T convention US_MEDIAN (median of jurisdiction estimates incl. territories), and the answer states that it is a median, not a pooled national prevalence.
tool_scope.subgroups: at most one break_out (category, value) from catalog/indicators.json
must_abstain: jurisdiction not in the 2025 file (e.g. CA, MS, NV) or sub-state geography (county/city)
age-adjusted or any statistic other than crude prevalence (means, medians of a variable, counts, trends, regressions)
more than one subgroup filter or a subgroup not in the catalog
questions that are not about the survey data

questions.authoring: hand-written with varied phrasing; gold spec assigned by hand from the catalog; reference value = CDC P&T snapshot cell for the gold spec
questions.dev_use: prompt and template-matcher iteration (at most 3 prompt revisions)
questions.test_use: frozen; run once per policy after the prompt and matcher are frozen at a recorded commit
questions.reference_must_pass_gate0: test items whose reference cell is not reproduced in Gate 0 are excluded from the primary analysis and reported separately
questions.stress_set: written after first held-out results (paraphrases, ambiguous denominators, wrong year/geography, subgroup traps, national-vs-median); reported separately, never part of the primary comparison

metrics.spec_exact_match: indicator, response, geography and subgroup all equal the gold spec (for should-abstain items: tool abstained)
metrics.numeric_agreement: tool executed an estimate and |estimate - CDC value| <= 0.1 pp
metrics.outcome_correct: PRIMARY ENDPOINT. Answerable item: numeric_agreement. Should-abstain item: tool abstained.
metrics.abstention: precision and recall with 'abstain' as the positive class
metrics.cost: USD per question from logged prompt/completion/cached tokens and docs/pricing.json
metrics.latency: wall-clock seconds per question incl. execution; median and p95; cached replays report the originally logged latency

policies.EXPERT: gold spec executed by the deterministic pipeline (the expert-specified process; no NL interpretation)
policies.TEMPLATE: deterministic keyword/regex matcher only; abstains when not confident
policies.ROUTER: TEMPLATE if it returns a confident spec; otherwise gpt-4o; escalate to gpt-4.1 if the gpt-4o spec is rejected by the guard or gpt-4o reports confidence 'low'
policies.GPT52: optional exploratory: gpt-5.2 on a subset only if capacity allows; never part of the primary comparison

noninferiority.comparison: ROUTER vs EXPERT on the held-out test split
noninferiority.method: paired difference ROUTER - EXPERT; Newcombe (1998) method 10 hybrid score 95% CI
noninferiority.decision: non-inferior if the lower 95% limit > -7.5 pp; otherwise 'not shown non-inferior'
secondary: ROUTER vs GPT41 cost and latency (descriptive)
